research_question: At a fixed search budget, does explicitly exploring candidate moves with different chess features help a small AlphaZero-style agent recover correct moves that its own initial policy ranks low?
creativity_definition: Operational and narrow: discovering a solution that was initially unlikely under the agent's own policy but is verified correct by an exact oracle. No claim of novelty to humanity, artistic merit, or general creative intelligence.
primary_endpoint: fraction of held-out test tasks where the selected root move is a member of the exactly-verified complete solution set
primary_comparison: feature-diverse allocation vs standard PUCT, paired on positions
verdict_rule: positive if the 95% family-clustered bootstrap CI of the paired difference lies entirely above zero; negative if entirely below; otherwise inconclusive
secondary_endpoints: success restricted to positions whose every verified solution falls outside the common raw-policy top three (same denominator for all methods)
policy rank and probability of the selected correct move
success as a function of search budget
search time and network evaluations per solved task
candidate coverage and feature dispersion (mechanism diagnostics only)
budget_accounting: Every condition is charged the full logical cost of the screening search it requires, even when one physical screen is reused; feature-computation wall time is added to the feature-diverse condition. No condition inherits another's search tree or any oracle result.
inclusion_criteria: solver_status == 'ok' and a legal selected move
exclusion_criteria: tasks whose exact solution set could not be completely enumerated

statistics.resampling_unit: source family (independent playout game or endgame seed)
statistics.seed_aggregation: repeated seeds averaged within a position before comparison

example_selection_rule: feature_win -> standard_win -> both_solved -> both_failed -> vs_random, up to 2 per category and 10 total, task-id order within a category

dataset.split_unit: source family (one playout game or one endgame construction seed)

checkpoint.frozen: the identical checkpoint is used for every condition

development_calibration.selection_rule: highest DEV success rate; ties broken toward the smaller lambda

no_test_tuning: all hyper-parameters were fixed from development data before any test score was computed; no seed selection was performed
